question: Which repos should this skill work for?
When the agent needs to file an issue on a foreign repo, what should it do FIRST? Should the skill define a step-by-step checklist or a more flexible guide?
For Step 1 (read CONTRIBUTING.md) — what exactly should the agent do? Read the full file? Just grep for specific keywords?

When checking for duplicates before filing — what's the bar? The agent should search open issues via `gh issue list` (if they have the repo cloned), or use `gh search issues` (no clone needed)? And how aggressively?
What sections should the generated issue body always include? Pick the closest set.

What qualifies as a "reproducible example" for this skill? The issue body says "be neutral, do not use examples from our own codebase" — meaning the repro must use generic/neutral examples, not cheasee-pi code.
If the target repo has NO CONTRIBUTING.md and NO issue templates at all, what should the skill instruct the agent to do?
What tone/formatting rules should the skill enforce for the issue body?
For Step 5 (file the issue) — should the skill include the exact `gh issue create` command template, or just instruct the agent to file without prescribing the CLI syntax?
What should this skill explicitly exclude? (Pick all that apply — I'll ask one at a time, start with the most important)
Should the skill exclude filing issues on our own repo (SchneiderDaniel/cheasee-pi)? Other skills (bug-hunter, reinvention-hunter) already handle that.
Public repos only, or support private repos too (requires gh auth to have access)?
If duplicate check finds a similar open issue, what should the skill instruct?
What tooling should the skill assume is available? `gh` is the core requirement. Should it also assume `jq` and `curl`?
After discussing all these topics — does anything else come to mind that you'd now like to add as a requirement?
